**Frontend (`apps/studio`)**

- `types.ts`: `ConnectorConfig`, `ConnectorPreset`, `ConnectorHealth`; `studioApi.ts`: `listConnectors`, `addConnectorPreset`, `addConnectorManual`, `removeConnector`, `healthConnector`; `sse.ts`: parse the new `connector` event; `ChatCopilot`: render a `connector_suggestion` card from chat and call `addConnectorPreset` on accept.
- No new dependencies (FastMCP already in `connectors`; `openai` already in `studio-api`).

**Tests** (per `.agents/workflows/test.md`, in-memory `fastmcp.Client` patterns): `apps/studio-api/tests/test_studio_connectors.py` + chat tool-call branch; `apps/studio/src/api/studio_connectors.test.ts` + `sse.test.ts`. Run `uv run ruff check . && uv run mypy apps packages && uv run pytest`, plus `npm --prefix studio run test`.

**Docs** (same task, per README guardrail): extend `docs/connectors.md` (Studio UI section) + `README.md` Code Overview (studio connector settings).

### Execution order
A first (license PR), then a short written design + plan for B (I'll follow the `writing-plans` flow), then implement B incrementally with tests, and finish with a PR per worktree convention.

This is the complete plan. Say the word and I'll switch out of plan mode and **start with A (license worktree + PR)**.

--- **Agentic ODI** explores how the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) can turn [Outcome-Driven Innovation](https://strategyn.com/outcome-driven-innovation/) into a live, agent-queryable source of context. This repository is an experimental testbed for understanding server–client MCP communication streams, built on [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp). We don't publish dates. This page changes when the code does. ## Code Overview A [uv workspace](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) of six installable Python projects plus the React `studio/` front end, each with its own build, tests, and layout: | Package | Description | |---|---| | **`core/`** (`agentic-odi-core`) | Domain models, the `ODIService` business-logic layer, and repository implementations (in-memory and SQLite), including ODI opportunity-score computation. | | **`mcp_server/`** (`agentic-odi-mcp-server`) | A foundational MCP Server exposing an HTTP transport layer. Ships as a browser SPA and as a **Tauri 2 desktop app** (`studio/src-tauri/`). | +| **`apps/studio/`** (React + TypeScript + Vite) | **The Living Studio** front end — a spatial, conversational GUI for Outcome-Driven Innovation with an interactive Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, WYSIWYG Impact Simulation, and Causal Lineage inspection, paired with an autonomous copilot. The copilot renders **agent-composed cards inline** (scored outcomes, opportunity boards, bet simulations) from a closed catalog the SPA owns. Ships as a browser SPA and as a **Tauri 2 desktop app** (`apps/studio/src-tauri/`). | | **`cli/`** (`agentic-odi-cli`) | A [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based command-line interface with an interactive chat mode plus `version`, `update`, `connectors`, and `customer-outcomes` (alias `outcomes`) commands. Data commands are local-first (`--backend local`, default) or remote (`--backend mcp`), with readable tables, `--json`, and a top-level `score`. | | **`connectors/`** (`agentic-odi-connectors`) | Pluggable external integrations. The first kind is an **MCP client connector** that connects to a remote MCP server over HTTP, checks health, and ingests tools/resources into a local ingest sink. Additional kinds (REST, webhooks, and so on) can register against the same protocol later. | ## Quick Start **Prerequisites:** Python 3.10+ and the [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) package manager. ```bash # Install the entire workspace (all six projects plus dev tooling) uv sync --all-packages # Build the Studio SPA, then launch the MCP server and Living Studio together npm --prefix studio run build python -m client.run ``` | Service | URL | |---|---| | MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp | | The Living Studio | http://127.0.0.1:8100 | For hot reload, `npm --prefix studio run dev:full` starts the MCP server, the sidecar, and Vite together on http://localhost:5173. For the desktop app, use `npm --prefix studio run tauri dev`. See [Running The Living Studio](docs/living-studio.md). The Studio needs an OpenAI-compatible LLM with tool-calling support to drive its agent — see the [Local LLM Backend](docs/local-llm.md). ### CLI at a glance The CLI is local-first, so data commands work without a running server: ```bash python -m cli --version # print the Agentic ODI version python -m cli --help # show available options and commands python -m cli # start interactive chat in a terminal agentic-odi customer-outcomes list agentic-odi score 8 2 # ODI opportunity score → 14.00 ``` Add `--backend mcp` to route data commands through a running MCP server (`python -m mcp_server`). +"""Validation and tool schema generation for agent-composed UI.
+
+The sidecar is deliberately catalog-agnostic: the client sends the manifest of
+what it can render with each turn, and this module derives both the ``render_ui``
+tool schema and the validator from it. There is exactly one source of truth for
+the catalog, and it lives with the renderer that has to honour it.
+
+Errors returned by :meth:`UiCatalog.validate` are fed straight back to the model
+as the tool result, so a fumbled prop becomes a same-turn correction rather than
+a silent blank space in the conversation.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Any
+
+MAX_DEPTH = 12
+MAX_NODES = 200
+MAX_STRING_LENGTH = 2000
+MAX_CHILDREN = 32
+
+RENDER_UI_TOOL = "render_ui"
+
+
+def _is_number(value: Any) -> bool:
+    return isinstance(value, (int, float)) and not isinstance(value, bool)
+
+
+class UiCatalog:
+    """The client's renderable catalog, as a tool schema and a validator."""
+
+    def __init__(self, components: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
+        self._order: list[str] = []
+        self._components: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
+        for component in components:
+            if not isinstance(component, dict):
+                continue
+            name = component.get("type")
+            if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or name in self._components:
+                continue
+            self._order.append(name)
+            self._components[name] = component
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_manifest(cls, manifest: Any) -> UiCatalog | None:
+        """Build a catalog from a request manifest, or ``None`` if unusable."""
+        if not isinstance(manifest, dict):
+            return None
+        components = manifest.get("components")
+        if not isinstance(components, list):
+            return None
+        catalog = cls(components)
+        return catalog if catalog.types else None
+
+    @property
+    def types(self) -> list[str]:
+        return list(self._order)
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ schema
+
+    def tool_schema(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        return {
+            "type": "object",
+            "description": (
+                "One UI node. Put the content in `props` and nest layouts with "
+                "`children`. The component catalog is in the tool description."
+            ),
+            "properties": {
+                "type": {
+                    "type": "string",
+                    "enum": self.types,
+                    "description": "Which surface to render.",
+                },
+                "props": {
+                    "type": "object",
+                    "description": "Props for the chosen type, as described in the catalog.",
+                },
+                "children": {
+                    "type": "array",
+                    "items": {"type": "object"},
+                    "description": "Child nodes. Only layout types accept them.",
+                },
+            },
+            "required": ["type"],
+        }
+
+    def describe(self) -> str:
+        """Compact catalogue the model reads, one line per component."""
+        lines = []
+        for name in self._order:
+            component = self._components[name]
+            props_schema = component.get("props") or {}
+            required = set(props_schema.get("required") or [])
+            properties = props_schema.get("properties") or {}
+            props = ", ".join(
+                f"{prop}*" if prop in required else prop for prop in properties if prop != "actions"
+            )
+            description = component.get("description") or ""
+            children = " Children allowed." if component.get("acceptsChildren") else ""
+            actions = " Optional actions." if "actions" in properties else ""
+            lines.append(f"- {name}({props}) — {description}{children}{actions}")
+        return "\n".join(lines)
+
+    # -------------------------------------------------------------- validation
+
+    def validate(self, spec: Any) -> str | None:
+        """Return a human-readable problem, or ``None`` when the spec is valid."""
+        return self._validate_node(spec, 0, {"nodes": 0})
+
+    def _validate_node(self, node: Any, depth: int, state: dict[str, int]) -> str | None:
+        if depth > MAX_DEPTH:
+            return f"the UI tree is deeper than {MAX_DEPTH} levels"
+        state["nodes"] += 1
+        if state["nodes"] > MAX_NODES:
+            return f"the UI tree has more than {MAX_NODES} nodes"
+
+        if not isinstance(node, dict):
+            return "a UI node must be an object"
+
+        name = node.get("type")
+        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
+            return "a UI node needs a `type`"
+
+        component = self._components.get(name)
+        if component is None:
+            allowed = ", ".join(self.types)
+            return f"`{name}` is not a renderable type. Use one of: {allowed}"
+
+        props = node.get("props")
+        if props is None:
+            props = {}
+        if not isinstance(props, dict):
+            return f"`{name}.props` must be an object"
+
+        props_schema = component.get("props") or {}
+        problem = self._validate_props(props, props_schema, f"{name}.props")
+        if problem:
+            return problem
+
+        children = node.get("children")
+        if children is not None and not isinstance(children, list):
+            return f"`{name}.children` must be an array"
+        if children and not component.get("acceptsChildren"):
+            # Same tolerance as the client: stray children are dropped, not fatal.
+            return None
+        if children and len(children) > MAX_CHILDREN:
+            # The client rejects the whole tree past this ceiling, so reject here
+            # rather than let a surface that never renders look like a success.
+            return f"`{name}` accepts at most {MAX_CHILDREN} children"
+        for index, child in enumerate(children or []):
+            problem = self._validate_node(child, depth + 1, state)
+            if problem:
+                return f"child {index}: {problem}"
+
+        return None
+
+    def _validate_props(
+        self, props: dict[str, Any], schema: dict[str, Any], path: str
+    ) -> str | None:
+        properties = schema.get("properties") or {}
+        required = schema.get("required") or []
+
+        for name in required:
+            if name not in props:
+                return f"`{path}.{name}` is required"
+
+        for name, value in props.items():
+            prop_schema = properties.get(name)
+            if not isinstance(prop_schema, dict):
+                continue  # unknown props are stripped, matching the renderer
+            problem = self._validate_value(value, prop_schema, f"{path}.{name}")
+            if problem and name in required:
+                return problem
+
+        return None
+
+    def _validate_value(self, value: Any, schema: dict[str, Any], path: str) -> str | None:
+        enum = schema.get("enum")
+        if isinstance(enum, list):
+            if value not in enum:
+                return f"`{path}` must be one of: {', '.join(str(item) for item in enum)}"
+            return None
+
+        kind = schema.get("type")
+
+        if kind == "string":
+            if not isinstance(value, str):
+                return f"`{path}` must be a string"
+            if len(value) > MAX_STRING_LENGTH:
+                return f"`{path}` is longer than {MAX_STRING_LENGTH} characters"
+            return None
+
+        if kind in ("number", "integer"):
+            if not _is_number(value):
+                return f"`{path}` must be a number"
+            if kind == "integer" and float(value) != int(value):
+                return f"`{path}` must be an integer"
+            minimum = schema.get("minimum")
+            maximum = schema.get("maximum")
+            if minimum is not None and value < minimum:
+                return f"`{path}` must be at least {minimum}"
+            if maximum is not None and value > maximum:
+                return f"`{path}` must be at most {maximum}"
+            return None
+
+        if kind == "boolean":
+            return None if isinstance(value, bool) else f"`{path}` must be a boolean"
+
+        if kind == "array":
+            if not isinstance(value, list):
+                return f"`{path}` must be an array"
+            minimum_items = schema.get("minItems")
+            maximum_items = schema.get("maxItems")
+            if isinstance(minimum_items, int) and len(value) < minimum_items:
+                return f"`{path}` needs at least {minimum_items} items"
+            if isinstance(maximum_items, int) and len(value) > maximum_items:
+                return f"`{path}` allows at most {maximum_items} items"
+            item_schema = schema.get("items")
+            if isinstance(item_schema, dict):
+                for index, item in enumerate(value):
+                    problem = self._validate_value(item, item_schema, f"{path}[{index}]")
+                    if problem:
+                        return problem
+            return None
+
+        if kind == "object":
+            if not isinstance(value, dict):
+                return f"`{path}` must be an object"
+            return self._validate_props(value, schema, path)
+
+        return None
+
+
+__all__ = ["MAX_CHILDREN", "MAX_DEPTH", "MAX_NODES", "RENDER_UI_TOOL", "UiCatalog"]

+/**

+ *
+ * Two tiers, deliberately small: primitives for composition, cards for the ODI
+ * shapes worth naming. Cards are leaves on the wire but render internally with
+ * the same primitives, so the agent expresses intent ("score this outcome")
+ * rather than layout.
+ *
+ * This file is the single source of truth. `catalogManifest()` is what travels
+ * to the sidecar; `catalogPrompt()` is what the model reads.
+ */
+
+import { UI_LIMITS, toManifest, type UiCatalogEntry, type UiPropSchema } from "./protocol";
+
+const actionList: UiPropSchema = {
+  type: "array",
+  maxItems: UI_LIMITS.maxActions,
+  description:
+    "Buttons rendered under the surface. Each one sends its `intent` back to you as the user's next message.",
+  items: {
+    type: "object",
+    properties: {
+      label: {
+        type: "string",
+        description: "Short imperative label, two to four words. e.g. \"Simulate this bet\"",
+      },
+      intent: {
+        type: "string",
+        description: "The full message to send when clicked, written as the user would say it.",
+      },
+      tone: { enum: ["primary", "ghost"], description: "Use primary at most once per surface." },
+    },
+    required: ["label", "intent"],
+  },
+};
+
+const outcomeScores: Record<string, UiPropSchema> = {
+  importance: { type: "number", minimum: 0, maximum: 10 },
+  satisfaction: { type: "number", minimum: 0, maximum: 10 },

+    props.actions = actionList;
+  }
+  return {
+    type,
+    kind,
+    description,

+        items: {
+          type: "object",
+          properties: {
+            name: { type: "string" },
+            stage: {
+              enum: [
+                "define",
+                "locate",
+                "prepare",
+                "confirm",
+                "execute",
+                "monitor",
+                "modify",
+                "conclude",
+              ],
+            },
+            note: { type: "string" },
+          },
+          required: ["name"],
+        },
+      },
+    },
+    ["job", "steps"],
+  ),
+  entry(
+    "decision-record",
+    "leaf",
+    "A Product Decision Record: the bet, the outcome it serves, and why it was chosen.",
+    {
+      title: { type: "string" },
+      outcomeId: { type: "string" },
+      bet: { type: "string" },
+      rationale: { type: "string" },
+      status: { enum: ["proposed", "approved", "rejected"] },
+    },
+    ["title", "bet", "rationale"],
+  ),
+];
+
+const CATALOG_TYPES = new Set(CATALOG.map((component) => component.type));
+
+export function isKnownType(type: string): boolean {
+  return CATALOG_TYPES.has(type);
+}
+
+export function catalogManifest() {
+  return toManifest([...CATALOG]);
+}
+
+function formatProp(name: string, schema: UiPropSchema, required: boolean): string {
+  let type = schema.type ?? "value";
+  if (schema.enum) {
+    type = schema.enum.map((value) => `"${value}"`).join(" | ");
+  } else if (schema.type === "array") {
+    type = "array";
+  } else if (schema.type === "number" || schema.type === "integer") {
+    const bounds =
+      schema.minimum !== undefined && schema.maximum !== undefined
+        ? ` ${schema.minimum}–${schema.maximum}`
+        : "";
+    type = `${schema.type}${bounds}`;
+  }
+  return `${name}${required ? "" : "?"}: ${type}`;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Compact, human-readable catalog for the model. Descriptions are the contract:
+ * they tell the model *when* to reach for a component, not just what it takes.
+ */
+export function catalogPrompt(): string {
+  return CATALOG.map((component) => {
+    const required = new Set(component.props.required ?? []);
+    const props = Object.entries(component.props.properties ?? {})
+      .filter(([name]) => name !== "actions")
+      .map(([name, schema]) => formatProp(name, schema, required.has(name)))
+      .join(", ");
+    const children = component.acceptsChildren ? " Children allowed." : "";
+    const actions = "actions" in (component.props.properties ?? {})
+      ? " Optional actions."
+      : "";
+    return `- ${component.type}(${props}) — ${component.description}${children}${actions}`;
+  }).join("\n");
+}

 # Running The Living Studio
 
 **The Living Studio** is the conversational GUI for Outcome-Driven Innovation:
 an interactive Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, WYSIWYG Impact
 Simulation, and Causal Lineage inspection, paired with an autonomous agent
 connected to the MCP server.
 
 The Studio runs three ways. All of them serve the same SPA, which talks only to
 the sidecar on `http://127.0.0.1:8100` — the SPA never contacts MCP or the LLM
 directly.
 
 ## Architecture
 
 ```text
 ┌────────────────────────────┐  /api (JSON)  ┌───────────────────────────────┐
 │  Living Studio SPA         │ ────────────▶ │  local_server (sidecar)       │
 │  React + TS + Vite         │  /api/chat    │  FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:8100    │
 │  (browser or Tauri webview)│ ◀──────────── │  - config / health / canvas   │
 └────────────────────────────┘  SSE stream   │  - steps / outcomes (via MCP) │
                                              │  - /api/chat (LLM tool-loop)  │
                                              └───────────────┬───────────────┘
                                                              │ MCP (HTTP)
                                                              ▼
                                              ┌───────────────────────────────┐
                                              │  mcp_server  :8000/mcp        │
                                              └───────────────────────────────┘
                                                              ▲
                                                              │ OpenAI-compatible
                                              ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
                                              │  Your local LLM backend       │
                                              └───────────────────────────────┘
 ```
 
 ## 1. Web — production build (recommended for a quick look)
 
 ```bash
 npm --prefix studio run build   # build the SPA into studio/dist
 python -m client.run            # starts MCP :8000 + sidecar :8100
 ```
 
 | Service | URL |
 |---|---|
 | MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp |
 | Living Studio | http://127.0.0.1:8100 |
 
 `python -m client.run` starts both processes concurrently; press **Ctrl+C** to
 stop both.
 
 ## 2. Web — dev with hot reload
 
 Vite proxies `/api` to the sidecar:
 
 ```bash
 npm --prefix studio run dev:full   # MCP + sidecar + Vite together
 # open http://localhost:5173
 ```
 
 ## 3. Desktop — Tauri 2
 
 The app spawns the MCP server and sidecar itself:
 
 ```bash
 npm --prefix studio run tauri dev     # dev window
 npm --prefix studio run tauri build   # bundles: .deb / .AppImage (Linux), .app / .dmg (macOS), .msi / .exe (Windows)
 ```
 
 > [!NOTE]
 > **Tauri prerequisites.** The desktop build needs the WebKitGTK toolchain and
 > Rust 1.90+. On Debian/Ubuntu:
 >
 > ```bash
 > sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential pkg-config curl wget file \
 >   libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf xdg-utils libfuse2t64
 > ```
 >
 > The Tauri CLI ships as the `@tauri-apps/cli` npm dev dependency
 > (`npm --prefix studio run tauri`). The sidecar is launched with
 > `uv run python -m …` from the repository root; if the app cannot locate the
 > repo root, set `AGENTIC_ODI_REPO_ROOT`.
 
 ## Desktop signing & updater secrets
 
 Self-updating and code signing are **env-driven**: if a secret is absent, an
 unsigned artifact is produced instead of failing. CI reads these from GitHub
 Actions secrets.
 
 | Secret | Purpose |
 |---|---|
 | `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` | Signs updater artifacts (`.sig`) and the `latest.json` manifest. A tagged release fails loudly without it. Generate with `npm --prefix studio run tauri signer generate`. |
 | `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD` | Password for the private key (optional when the key has none). |
 | `APPLE_CERTIFICATE` / `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | macOS Developer ID certificate (base64 `.p12`) and its password. |
 | `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY` | macOS signing identity. |
 | `APPLE_ID` / `APPLE_PASSWORD` / `APPLE_TEAM_ID` | macOS notarization credentials. |
 | `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE` / `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | Windows Authenticode PFX (base64) and its password; imported by CI and injected into the bundle config. |
 
 Releases are published by `.github/workflows/tauri-release.yml` when a `v*` tag
 is pushed. The desktop app checks for updates on startup and via
 **Settings → Check for updates**.
 
 ### Managing the updater signing key
 
 The updater key pair authenticates release artifacts so an installed app can
 verify that an auto-update genuinely came from you. The **public** key is
 embedded in `studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` (`plugins.updater.pubkey`) and is
 safe to commit. The **private** key must never be committed, logged, printed in
 CI, or attached to a build artifact.
 
 1. **Generate a key pair** (only if you need a new one). Leave `-p ""` for a
    passwordless key, or pass a password and remember it:
 
    ```bash
    npm --prefix studio run tauri signer generate -- -w ./living-studio.key -p "" -f
    ```
 
    This writes `living-studio.key` (private, `0600`) and `living-studio.key.pub`
    (public).
 
 2. **Paste the public key** into `studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`:
 
    ```jsonc
    {
      "plugins": {
        "updater": {
          "endpoints": ["https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/latest.json"],
          "pubkey": "<contents of living-studio.key.pub>"
        }
      }
    }
    ```
 
 3. **Store the private key outside the repository** (the repo root is
    git-tracked; a sibling directory is not), with restricted permissions:
 
    ```bash
    mkdir -p ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys && chmod 700 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys
    mv living-studio.key ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/
    chmod 600 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key
    ```
 
    Move it to a long-term secret store (password manager, 1Password/Bitwarden/
    Vault, or a private encrypted backup) when you decide where that lives.
    Losing it means future releases can no longer be signed for existing
    installs.
 
 4. **Add the private key as a GitHub Actions secret** (Settings → Secrets and
    variables → Actions → New repository secret), or via the CLI:
 
    ```bash
    gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY < ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key
    gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD --body ""   # only if you set a password
    ```
 
 5. **Verify** the secrets exist (values are never displayed):
 
    ```bash
    gh secret list
    ```
 
 6. **Rotate** by repeating steps 1–4, then publishing a release signed with the
    new key. Existing installs still verify against the public key compiled into
    their binary, so keep the old private key usable and publish the new public
    key ahead of the cut-over.
 
 > [!CAUTION]
 > If the private key leaks, treat auto-updates as compromised: generate a new
 > pair, rotate the Actions secret, and publish a freshly signed release.
 
 > [!IMPORTANT]
 > **Migration note.** The Streamlit UI (`client/src/client/app.py`) has been
 > removed. The Living Studio now lives in `studio/` (browser SPA + Tauri desktop
 > app) and is served by the `local_server` sidecar on port **8100** (previously
 > Streamlit's `8501`). Start everything with `python -m client.run`. All
 > `AGENTIC_ODI_*` environment variable names, the demo dataset, and the ODI
 > formulas are unchanged.
 
+## Rich responses
+
+The copilot does not only talk. When a surface carries the evidence better than a
+paragraph, the agent renders one **inline in the conversation**: a scored
+outcome, a ranked opportunity board, a before/after simulation of a bet, a
+customer quote with its lineage, the eight-stage job map, or a decision record.
+Three properties keep this safe and cheap to extend:
+
+- **The catalog is closed and owned by the SPA.**
+  `apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts` declares nine primitives and six cards, their
+  JSON Schema props, and the description the model reads. There is no HTML, no
+  eval, and no third-party component in the path.
+- **The sidecar is catalog-agnostic.** The SPA sends the catalog with each turn;
+  the sidecar derives the `render_ui` tool schema from it, validates what comes
+  back, and streams a `ui` SSE event. Invalid props return to the model as a tool
+  result naming the exact violation, so a fumbled prop is corrected in the same
+  reply. A client that sends no catalog never sees the tool.
+- **Cards are views, never actors.** Every button is an `intent` string that the
+  agent receives as the user's next message — one authority, one audit trail.
+
+A surface is one node tree, streamed as one event:
+
+```json
+{
+  "type": "outcome-card",
+  "props": {
+    "id": "O-1",
+    "statement": "Minimize the time it takes to propagate secrets across environments",
+    "importance": 9,
+    "satisfaction": 3
+  }
+}
+```
+
+The opportunity score is computed from importance and satisfaction when the
+agent omits it, so the ODI formula has exactly one home (`src/lib/odi.ts`).
+Unknown component types degrade to a quiet fallback; a tree that fails
+validation is dropped whole, and the surrounding prose still reads.
+
+Run the sidecar without a model and the demo still renders real cards — that
+path is what a first-run user sees, and it exercises every card type in CI.
+
+### Adding a surface
+
+1. Add an entry to `CATALOG` in `apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts` — props as a
+   JSON Schema subset, plus the description the model will read.
+2. Register the component in `apps/studio/src/ui/registry.ts`.
+3. Implement it in `apps/studio/src/ui/cards.tsx` (domain shape) or
+   `apps/studio/src/ui/primitives.tsx` (composition).
+4. Run `npm --prefix apps/studio test`. The `registry parity` test fails if the
+   catalog and the registry drift apart.
+
+No server change is needed, and no new dependency.
+
 ## Connecting an LLM
 
 The Studio needs an OpenAI-compatible LLM backend with tool-calling support to
 drive the agent. For a fully local setup, see
 [Local LLM Backend](local-llm.md).
 
 ## Agent-Driven Testing
 
 Type `/dev` in the AI assistant to trigger the full automated workflow: it starts
 both processes, opens the browser, sends a test message, and reports the results.
 
 Type `/test` to have the agent run all tests and report the results
 automatically.

   intelligently request customer insights when ideating features.

+# Conversational Generative UI — implementation plan
+
+**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-21-conversational-generative-ui-design.md`
+**Goal:** The agent composes validated rich surfaces from a closed catalog, rendered
+inline in the transcript, with actions that return intents to the agent.
+
+**Tech:** React 19 + TS + Vite + vitest (no new deps); FastAPI + pydantic (no new deps);
+JSON Schema (draft 2020-12 subset) as the single wire contract.
+
+**Execution note:** no subagent tool is available in this harness, so tasks run inline
+in order.
+
+---
+
+## Task 1 — Client protocol (`apps/studio/src/ui/protocol.ts`)
+
+Types `UiSpec`, `UiNode`, `UiPropSchema`, `UiCatalogManifest`. Implements
+`parseUiSpec(raw, manifest)` → `{ ok: true, node } | { ok: false, reason }`:
+
+- structural checks (object, `type` string, `props` object, `children` array)
+- limits: depth 12, 200 nodes, 2000-char strings, 32 children, 40 actions
+- catalog lookup; unknown type → retained as `{ type, props: {} }` marked unsupported
+- per-prop validation: `string | number | boolean | integer`, `enum`, `minimum`,
+  `maximum`, `items`, `minItems`/`maxItems`, nested `object` fields, `required`
+- unknown props stripped
+
+Tests: valid tree accepted; unknown type tolerated; wrong prop type rejected; depth and
+node ceilings enforced; children rejected on leaves; unknown props stripped; non-object
+rejected.
+
+## Task 2 — Catalog manifest (`apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts`)
+
+`CATALOG` — 9 primitives + 6 cards, each `{ type, kind, description, acceptsChildren,
+actions?, props: JSONSchema }`. `catalogManifest()` returns the serializable projection
+sent to the sidecar. `catalogPrompt()` returns the human-readable block used in the
+system prompt and tool description.
+
+Tests: unique type names; every entry has a description; `catalogManifest()` is
+JSON-round-trippable; every card accepts `actions`; only layout nodes accept children.
+
+## Task 3 — Primitives (`apps/studio/src/ui/primitives.tsx`)
+
+`Stack`, `Grid`, `Heading`, `Text`, `ListBlock`, `Stat`, `Meter`, `Callout`, `Divider`,
+plus the shared `ActionRow`. All styling by class name against `theme.css`.
+
+## Task 4 — Cards (`apps/studio/src/ui/cards.tsx`)
+
+`OutcomeCard`, `OpportunityBoard`, `ImpactSimulation`, `EvidenceQuote`, `JobMap`,
+`DecisionRecord`. Cards compute the ODI opportunity score from
+`lib/odi.ts` when `opportunityScore` is absent — the formula has one home.
+
+## Task 5 — Renderer (`apps/studio/src/ui/UiRenderer.tsx`, `registry.ts`)
+
+`NODE_COMPONENTS` maps type → component. `UiRenderer` walks the tree recursively,
+wraps each node in a boundary, resolves actions through `UiActionContext`.
+`UnknownNode` fallback names the unknown type.
+
+Tests: renders an outcome card with computed score; unknown type renders a fallback that
+names it; clicking an action calls `onIntent` with the intent text; a throwing card does
+not kill siblings; actions disabled while busy.
+
+## Task 6 — Inline-markdown (`apps/studio/src/ui/RichText.tsx`)
+
+Paragraphs, `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `` `code` ``, `[label](url)`, `- ` bullets, `###`
+headings. No HTML injection path. Tests cover each construct and escaping.
+
+## Task 7 — Chat state (`types.ts`, `StudioContext.tsx`)
+
+`ChatPart`, `UiSpec`, extended `ChatMessage`/`ChatStreamRequest`. `sendMessage` builds
+parts; `ui` SSE events append `{kind:"ui"}` parts; `message` events replace text parts;
+`onIntent` reuses `sendMessage`. Welcome message becomes a designed first-run card.
+
+## Task 8 — Chat surface (`ChatCopilot.tsx`)
+
+Render parts in order; text through `RichText`, UI through `UiRenderer`; compact
+activity rail; keep ⌘K, Enter-to-send, auto-scroll.
+
+## Task 9 — Sidecar (`studio/ui_spec.py`, `schemas.py`, `chat.py`, `offline_ui.py`)
+
+`UiCatalog` from the request manifest; `tool_schema()`; `validate(spec)`; `render_ui`
+local tool intercepted in the loop; `ui` SSE event; `canvas_dirty` only for MCP calls;
+offline demo emitting real cards.
+
+Tests: manifest → tool schema; validation accepts/rejects; chat emits `ui` for a valid
+spec and a corrective tool result for an invalid one; offline cards validate against a
+fixture catalog.
+
+## Task 10 — Style and verification
+
+`theme.css` card surfaces, score tones, meters, motion, reduced motion. Then:
+`npm --prefix apps/studio run typecheck`, `… run lint`, `… run test`,
+`uv run --directory apps/studio-api pytest`, plus root `ruff`.
+
+## Task 11 — Docs
+
+`README.md` (capability line) and `docs/living-studio.md` (Rich responses section),
+`docs/roadmap.md` if applicable.

+# Conversational Generative UI for The Living Studio — design
+
+**Status:** approved for implementation
+**Date:** 2026-10-21
+**Scope:** `apps/studio` (React SPA + Tauri) and `apps/studio-api` (FastAPI sidecar)
+
+## Intent
+
+The Studio's agent is its product. Today that agent's intelligence is trapped in
+prose: it can reason about an opportunity landscape, but it can only *describe*
+the landscape. Everything it knows arrives as a wall of text in a `pre-wrap`
+bubble, so the user has to read, translate, and then go click a canvas tab to
+see the thing they were just told about.
+
+The conversational experience should let the agent **hand you things**. When it
+scores an outcome, you get the outcome card. When it pressure-tests a bet, you
+get the before/after simulation. When it cites a customer, you get the quote with
+its lineage. Prose introduces the artifact; the artifact carries the evidence.
+
+That is the whole idea. Everything below exists to make it safe, modular, and
+quiet enough to feel effortless.
+
+## Goals
+
+1. The agent can compose rich surfaces from a **closed, typed catalog** — no
+   HTML, no eval, no arbitrary code, ever.
+2. Rich surfaces render **inline in the transcript**, interleaved with prose in
+   the order the agent produced them.
+3. The catalog is **owned by the client** and published to the sidecar per
+   request, so there is exactly one source of truth.
+4. Every card can offer **actions**, which dispatch a typed intent back to the
+   agent. Cards are views, never actors.
+5. Degradation is graceful and total: unknown type → a quiet fallback node;
+   unparseable spec → the prose still reads; no LLM → a designed demo that still
+   shows real cards.
+
+## Non-goals
+
+- **No third-party/remote catalogs.** The catalog ships with the app. The wire
+  format is compatible with a future A2UI-style multi-catalog world, but v1 does
+  not accept a catalog from anywhere but the trusted client build.
+- **No direct data mutation from cards.** Actions produce prompts. The agent
+  keeps the single authority and the single audit trail.
+- **No prose-embedded UI extraction.** Guessing at fenced blocks in model output
+  reintroduces a second, unvalidated protocol path. One path only.
+- **No WYSIWYG layout editor.** The agent composes; the human reacts.
+
+## Architecture
+
+Three layers and one contract.
+
+```
+┌──────────────────────────── apps/studio (React) ────────────────────────────┐
+│                                                                             │
+│  ui/catalog.ts        ui/protocol.ts        ui/UiRenderer.tsx               │
+│  ┌────────────┐       ┌─────────────┐       ┌──────────────────┐            │
+│  │ 15 nodes   │──────▶│ validate +  │──────▶│ registry lookup  │            │
+│  │ + schemas  │       │ normalize   │       │ + ErrorBoundary  │            │
+│  │ + prompts  │       │ + limits    │       │ + action context │            │
+│  └────────────┘       └─────────────┘       └──────────────────┘            │
+│         │                                          │                        │
+│         │ catalogManifest()                        ▼                        │
+│         ▼                                  ui/primitives.tsx               │
+│   ChatStreamRequest.ui_catalog             ui/cards.tsx                     │
+└──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
+                               │ POST /api/chat  (SSE)
+                               ▼
+┌──────────────────── apps/studio-api (FastAPI) ──────────────────────────────┐
+│  studio/ui_spec.py        studio/chat.py              studio/offline_ui.py  │
+│  ┌──────────────────┐     ┌──────────────────┐        ┌──────────────────┐  │
+│  │ UiCatalog        │     │ tool loop:       │        │ designed demo    │  │
+│  │ .tool_schema()   │────▶│  render_ui is a  │───────▶│ cards for the    │  │
+│  │ .validate()      │     │  local tool, not │        │ no-LLM path      │  │
+│  │ (JSON Schema)    │     │  an MCP tool     │        └──────────────────┘  │
+│  └──────────────────┘     └──────────────────┘                              │
+└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
+```
+
+The sidecar is **catalog-agnostic**. It receives a manifest, derives the
+`render_ui` tool schema and a validation surface from it, and never hardcodes a
+component name. Swap the client, and the server still works.
+
+### Why the catalog lives on the client
+
+Because presentation is a client concern, and because the alternative — a shared
+JSON file consumed by a Vite build and a Python wheel — is a packaging problem
+waiting to drift. The sidecar is a local trust boundary; the client already
+declares its capabilities in the request body. If no manifest is sent (CLI,
+scripts, older clients), the server simply does not offer `render_ui`.
+
+### The contract
+
+A UI payload is a tree:
+
+```json
+{
+  "type": "outcome-card",
+  "props": {
+    "id": "O-1",
+    "statement": "Minimize the time it takes to propagate secrets across environments",
+    "importance": 9,
+    "satisfaction": 3
+  },
+  "children": []
+}
+```
+
+- `type` names a catalog entry. Unknown types are dropped with a visible,
+  non-alarming fallback — never silently rendered as blank space.
+- `props` are validated against that entry's JSON Schema subset. Unknown keys are
+  stripped, not trusted.
+- `children` is only legal on layout nodes; stray children on a leaf card are
+  dropped rather than allowed to lose the card.
+- Nesting happens **only** through `children`. Props never contain nodes.
+
+The manifest is plain JSON Schema (`draft 2020-12` subset: `type`, `properties`,
+`required`, `enum`, `minimum`/`maximum`, `items`, `minItems`/`maxItems`,
+`additionalProperties`). The same document is embedded verbatim in the tool
+schema and used to validate the result, so the model and the validator can never
+disagree about what is legal.
+
+### Catalog v1
+
+Two tiers, deliberately small. Tens of components is a design system; fifteen is
+a vocabulary.
+
+**Primitives (9)** — composition: `stack`, `grid`, `heading`, `text`, `list`,
+`stat`, `meter`, `callout`, `divider`.
+
+**Cards (6)** — ODI shapes worth naming: `outcome-card`, `opportunity-board`,
+`impact-simulation`, `evidence-quote`, `job-map`, `decision-record`.
+
+Cards are leaves as far as the wire format goes, but they render internally using
+the same primitives. The agent expresses *intent* (`score this outcome`), not
+*layout*. Novel shapes compose from primitives.
+
+**Actions** are a prop, not a node: `actions: [{ label, intent, tone? }]`. Any
+component may hold them; the renderer places them in a footer row. One shape,
+one renderer, no special cases.
+
+### Protocol limits
+
+Generation is untrusted by construction, so the parser enforces ceilings before
+anything touches React: max depth 12, max 200 nodes, max 2000-character strings,
+max 40 actions per node, max 32 children per node. Over-limit input is rejected
+as a whole — partial rendering of a runaway tree is worse than none.
+
+### Streaming model
+
+A new SSE event:
+
+```
+event: ui
+data: {"id":"ui_3","spec":{...}}
+```
+
+It arrives atomically, after validation. The message model becomes ordered parts:
+
+```ts
+type ChatPart =
+  | { kind: "text"; text: string }
+  | { kind: "ui"; id: string; spec: UiSpec };
+
+interface ChatMessage { role: "user" | "assistant"; content: string; parts: ChatPart[] }
+```
+
+`content` is kept as the concatenation of text parts because it is what gets sent
+back as conversation history; `parts` is what gets rendered. History serialization
+stays byte-identical to today, so the LLM sees no change in its transcript.
+
+### Server tool loop
+
+The sidecar already fans MCP tools into the completion. It gains one **local**
+tool, `render_ui`, bound before the MCP call and intercepted after:
+
+- valid spec → `event: ui`, tool result `"Rendered."`
+- invalid spec → no event, tool result names the exact schema violation
+
+The corrective tool result is the whole retry mechanism. No second prompt, no
+retry budget, no silent failure — a local model that fumbles a prop gets told
+which prop, in the same turn.
+
+`canvas_dirty` is now emitted only when an actual MCP tool ran.
+
+### No-LLM path
+
+`offline_fallback` grows into `offline_ui.py`: a designed demo that emits real
+cards — the eight universal job-map stages as a `job-map`, an opportunity board
+with computed scores, and a before/after simulation. A new user with no model
+configured still sees what the product is. This also gives every card type a
+live example in CI.
+
+### Interaction
+
+`UiActionContext` carries `{ onIntent, busy }` from the chat surface into the
+renderer. Clicking an action calls `sendMessage(intent)` — disabled while a
+response is streaming. The card never reaches into canvas state, never mutates
+data, never knows what an MCP tool is.
+
+### Failure isolation
+
+Every rendered node is wrapped in a boundary. A card that throws degrades to a
+`callout` saying so, and the rest of the transcript survives. Rendering is pure:
+no node can trigger network I/O on mount.
+
+## The experience
+
+What Jobs would have vetoed, and what replaces it:
+
+| Before | After |
+| --- | --- |
+| `### WYSIWYG Impact Simulation` rendered literally, with `**` and `-` | Real headings, real lists, real emphasis — a small, safe inline-markdown renderer |
+| A 480px scroll box of identically-shaped grey bubbles | Cards that are visibly *different kinds of thing*, with hierarchy and weight |
+| Every outcome described in prose, then clicked for elsewhere | The outcome card *is* the answer, with its score, its formula, and its lineage |
+| A permanent amber `🛠️` bubble per tool call | A quiet, collapsing activity rail that reads as status, not output |
+| Generic indigo buttons everywhere | One primary action per card, secondary actions quiet |
+
+Motion is one honest gesture: a card rises 6px and fades in over ~220ms with a
+40ms stagger across siblings, and the whole motion block is removed under
+`prefers-reduced-motion`.
+
+Accessibility is not a later pass: the transcript is a `role="log"` live region,
+cards are `article`s with `aria-label`s, meters expose `role="meter"` with
+`aria-valuenow`/`aria-valuemin`/`aria-valuemax`, actions are real `<button>`s with
+visible focus rings, and the fallback node is announced rather than hidden.
+
+## Constraints
+
+- No new runtime dependencies. The validator, the markdown renderer, and every
+  card are hand-written against the existing React 19 / Vite / vitest stack.
+- Python 3.10+, `pydantic`, no new packages.
+- Rules of the house: tests per package with the workspace `uv` layout, README
+  and `docs/living-studio.md` updated in the same change.
+
+## What is left to the builder
+
+Exact CSS values, animation curves beyond the described feel, the internal
+composition of each card, and the precise wording of the catalog descriptions
+the model reads. These are craft decisions, not contract decisions.

@@ -0,0 +1,204 @@
+# Design: MCP Connector Integration for The Living Studio
+
+**Date:** 2026-10-21
+**Topic:** Expose the existing MCP *client* connectors in the Living Studio (config, UI, conversational suggestions)
+**Status:** Draft → build (approved by human in chat)
+
+## What exists today
+
+The `packages/connectors/` package already implements the MCP **client** side of
+this story:
+
+- `mcp/connector.py` — `MCPClientConnector` using `fastmcp.Client` over HTTP,
+  with `${VAR}` credential expansion and OAuth token support.
+- `catalog.py` — 16 curated presets across 5 capability areas, with
+  `get_preset`, `list_presets(area)`, `connector_config_from_preset`.
+- `registry.py` — `ConnectorRegistry`, JSON-backed, read/write of `connectors.json`.
+- `factory.py` — `build_connector(ConnectorConfig)`.
+- CLI `connectors list|catalog|add|health|ingest` in `apps/cli/src/.../connectors.py`.
+- `docs/connectors.md` documents the CLI flow.
+
+The gap is the **Studio side**: the sidecar (`apps/studio-api`) has no connector
+routes; `SettingsPanel.tsx` only shows *simulated* MCP sources; and the chat
+engine (`studio/chat.py`) connects to a single ODI `mcp_url` and cannot surface
+or wire a connector. This design fills that gap without re-architecting the
+connectors package.
+
+## Intent & why
+
+Let a PM connect an external MCP server (search, analytics, CRM, etc.) as a
+data source for ODI — from the Studio UI, or by asking the copilot in conversation —
+and have the choice persist to a shared background config file used by both the
+CLI and the Studio. "Modular" = keep using the existing `Connector` protocol and
+preset catalog; just surface it in two new places (Studio settings + chat).
+
+## Goals / non-goals / anti-goals
+
+- Goals:
+  - Shared background config file (CLI + Studio + Tauri all agree on the path).
+  - Studio UI: list configured connectors + live health, add from a curated
+    "Recommended" preset subset, add a custom URL, remove.
+  - Conversational: the copilot can *suggest and wire* a connector via a
+    sidecar-native tool call (your answer 2), surfaced as a UI suggestion card.
+- Non-goals:
+  - Auto-discovery/marketplace manifest fetching (your answer 3: presets are the
+    recommended set; a separate "add custom" experience covers self-hosted /
+    external-marketplace servers). Defer live external marketplace discovery.
+  - Ingest-from-Studio mapping onto ODI artifacts (already deferred in roadmap).
+  - Making the ODI *server* expose connector tools (the sidecar owns config,
+    not the ODI server).
+- Anti-goal: do not couple the ODI server to the connectors package.
+
+## Locked decisions (from the human)
+
+1. **Shared config file:** sidecar and CLI share one file.
+2. **Conversational behavior:** the LLM *calls a sidecar tool* to register/wire a
+   connector inline (one chat turn), not just text-suggest.
+3. **Marketplaces:** the most prominent hosted MCP servers are surfaced as easy
+   presets; users can still add arbitrary servers via a "add custom" flow.
+
+## Defaults decided by me (flagged)
+
+- **Config location:** `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_FILE` env →
+  `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/agentic-odi/connectors.json` (fallback `~/.config/agentic-odi/connectors.json`).
+  This matches the existing `llm_profile.json` XDG location and works regardless of
+  cwd (important for the Tauri sidecar). The CLI default changes from cwd-relative
+  `.agentic-odi/connectors.json` to this resolver; CLI tests use `--config`/tmp so
+  they are unaffected. I'll update `docs/connectors.md` to match.
+- **Recommended subset:** I'll add an `is_recommended: bool = False` field to
+  `ConnectorPreset` and mark these (prominent, mostly API-key or OAuth-hosted):
+  `exa`, `tavily`, `posthog`, `amplitude`, `github`, `linear`, `slack`. The CLI
+  `connectors catalog` gains a `--recommended` flag too. (Call to confirm below.)
+- **MIT copyright:** `Copyright (c) 2026 Agentic ODI contributors` (already applied
+  in PR #54).
+
+## Architecture
+
+```text
+                                         ┌──────────────────────────────┐
+  Living Studio SPA (settings &         │ agentic_odi_studio_api       │
+  connector cards) ── /api/connectors ─▶│ - studio/connectors.py  (NEW)  │
+                                      │   list/add/remove/health on the│
+                                      │   shared ConnectorRegistry        │
+                                      │ - studio/router.py        (EXT)   │
+                                      │   GET/POST/DELETE endpoints       │
+  ┌───────────────────┐ /api/chat      │ - studio/chat.py       (EXT)    │
+  │   ChatCopilot     │ SSE:           │   native tool-call: add_connector│
+  │  suggestion card  │ connector event│   → registry.write + health     │
+  └───────────────────┘ canvas_dirty   └──────────┬──────────────────────┘
+                                  MCP/HTTP ▼        │
+                            mcp_server (:8000)      ▼
+                                  connectors package (catalog/presets),
+                                  shared connectors.json (~/.config/agentic-odi/)
+```
+
+The ODI `mcp_server` is untouched. The sidecar owns connector config + health.
+
+## Sidecar: `studio/connectors.py` (new)
+
+A thin service layer over the existing connectors package; importable and
+unit-testable without HTTP:
+
+- `connectors_file() -> Path` — delegates to a new
+  `agentic_odi_connectors.paths.connectors_file()` resolver (shared with CLI).
+- `list_connectors() -> list[ConnectorConfig]`
+- `list_catalog(area: str | None = None, recommended: bool = False) -> list[ConnectorPreset]`
+- `add_from_preset(preset_id, name=None) -> AddedConnector` (registers via
+  `connector_config_from_preset` + `ConnectorRegistry.add`, then runs
+  `connector.health()` and includes the result)
+- `add_manual(name, url, headers=None) -> AddedConnector`
+- `remove_connector(name) -> None`
+- `health(name) -> HealthStatus` (builds the connector and awaits `health()`)
+
+`AddedConnector` = `{config, health}`. Health failures (missing env, unreachable)
+are caught and returned (not raised), so the UI shows a red dot + message.
+
+## Sidecar: `router.py` (extend)
+
+- `GET /api/connectors` → `list_connectors()`
+- `GET /api/connectors/catalog?area=&recommended=` → presets
+- `POST /api/connectors` body `{preset_id? | name+url+headers?}` → add (returns
+  `{ok, name, kind, health}`)
+- `DELETE /api/connectors/{name}` → remove
+- `POST /api/connectors/{name}/health` → `{ok, message, details}`
+
+Routes resolve the file per-request (stateless); env override works for tests and
+Tauri.
+
+## Chat engine: `studio/chat.py` (extend)
+
+Today `stream_chat` builds LLM tools from `mcp_client.list_tools()` (ODI tools)
+only. Extension:
+
+- Define two **sidecar-native** tool schemas (NOT on the ODI server):
+  `add_connector_from_preset(preset_id, name?)` and `add_connector_manual(name,
+  url, headers?)`. Append them to the OpenAI `tools` list alongside the MCP tools.
+- When the LLM emits tool_calls, branch: if `name` is a native tool, execute it
+  via `connectors.add_from_preset`/`add_manual` (locally, no `mcp_client`); else
+  `mcp_client.call_tool(...)`.
+- On a successful native add, yield a new SSE event `connector` carrying
+  `{name, preset_id?, health}` so the UI renders a "Connected" card / toast, then
+  feed the human-readable result back into `messages` and continue to the final
+  stream as today.
+- The LLM is primed in `SYSTEM_PROMPT` to offer to connect an external source
+  when the user mentions one it knows (e.g., "Gong call" → suggest the `gong`
+  preset). It only calls the tool when the user consents in the same turn.
+
+One tool-call round (same shape as today); no multi-turn agentic loop added.
+
+## Frontend
+
+- `types.ts`: add `ConnectorConfig`, `ConnectorPreset`, `ConnectorHealth`,
+  `ConnectorSuggestion` (with `area`, `preset_id`).
+- `studioApi.ts`: `listConnectors`, `listPresets`, `addConnectorPreset`,
+  `addConnectorManual`, `removeConnector`, `healthConnector`.
+- `sse.ts`: already generic `event + data`; extend `RawSseEvent`-handling in
+  `StudioContext` to read a new `connector` event type.
+- `StudioContext.tsx`: add `connectors`, `presets`, and `addConnector*` state +
+  handlers; on `connector` SSE event, push a toast + refresh the connectors list.
+- `SettingsPanel.tsx`: new "Connectors" section —
+  - "Recommended" preset cards (the `is_recommended` subset) with Connect buttons;
+  - configured list with 🟢/🔴 health dots and ✕ remove;
+  - "Add custom" form (name, url, optional `KEY=VALUE` headers).
+- `ChatCopilot.tsx`: render a `connector` suggestion card in the chat log (next to

    calls: list[tuple[str, str, dict]] = []

    async def _call(mcp_url: str, tool: str, arguments: dict) -> str:

    response = _client().post(
        "/api/steps",
        json={"mcp_url": "http://mcp", "job_id": "job-1", "name": "Execute", "order": 5},

    assert response.json() == {"ok": True, "result": "step-1"}

def test_post_outcome_returns_the_mcp_result(monkeypatch) -> None:

                "importance": 8.5,

    ]

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from agentic_odi_connectors.catalog import (
    AREA_LABELS,
    PRESETS,
    UnknownAreaError,
    UnknownPresetError,
    connector_config_from_preset,
    get_preset,
    list_presets,
)
from agentic_odi_connectors.registry import ConnectorRegistry

ENV_REF = re.compile(r"\$\{([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}")


def test_preset_ids_are_unique() -> None:
    ids = [preset.id for preset in PRESETS]

    assert len(ids) == len(set(ids))


def test_every_capability_area_is_covered() -> None:
    assert {preset.area for preset in PRESETS} == set(AREA_LABELS)


def test_presets_use_https_endpoints_and_docs() -> None:
    for preset in PRESETS:
        assert preset.url.startswith("https://"), preset.id
        assert preset.docs.startswith("https://"), preset.id
        assert preset.summary, preset.id


def test_interpolated_env_vars_are_declared() -> None:
    for preset in PRESETS:
        referenced = set(ENV_REF.findall(preset.url))
        for value in preset.headers.values():
            referenced |= set(ENV_REF.findall(value))

        assert referenced <= set(preset.env_vars), preset.id


def test_oauth_presets_need_no_static_credentials() -> None:
    for preset in PRESETS:
        if preset.auth == "oauth":
            assert preset.env_vars == [], preset.id
            assert preset.headers == {}, preset.id


def test_api_key_presets_declare_credentials() -> None:
    for preset in PRESETS:
        if preset.auth != "oauth":
            assert preset.env_vars, preset.id


def test_list_presets_filters_by_area() -> None:
    filtered = list_presets("knowledge-output")

    assert filtered
    assert all(preset.area == "knowledge-output" for preset in filtered)


def test_list_presets_rejects_unknown_area() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(UnknownAreaError):
        list_presets("not-an-area")


def test_get_preset_unknown_raises() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(UnknownPresetError):
        get_preset("not-a-preset")


def test_connector_config_from_preset_populates_settings() -> None:
    preset = get_preset("github")

    config = connector_config_from_preset(preset)

    assert config.name == "github"
    assert config.kind == "mcp"
    assert config.enabled is True
    assert config.settings["url"] == preset.url
    assert config.settings["env_vars"] == ["GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN"]
    assert config.settings["headers"]["Authorization"] == ("Bearer ${GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN}")


def test_connector_config_from_preset_allows_overrides() -> None:
    preset = get_preset("linear")

    config = connector_config_from_preset(
        preset,
        name="team-linear",
        url="http://localhost:9000/mcp",
        tools=["list_issues"],
    )

    assert config.name == "team-linear"
    assert config.settings["url"] == "http://localhost:9000/mcp"
    assert config.settings["tools"] == ["list_issues"]


def test_registry_accepts_preset_config(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    registry = ConnectorRegistry(tmp_path / "connectors.json")

    registry.add(connector_config_from_preset(get_preset("notion")))

    stored = registry.get("notion")
    assert stored.settings["auth"] == "oauth"
    assert stored.settings["url"] == "https://mcp.notion.com/mcp"

But cwd for the sidecar is the repo root, so `.agentic-odi/connectors.json` would be in the repo root — not great for a "background config file."

I think the XDG approach is correct and the right call. I'll document it as my decision. The CLI tests use tmp_path so they won't break. The only "break" is if someone relied on cwd-relative `.agentic-odi/connectors.json` without setting the env — minor and documented.

For native `add_connector`, one round suffices: LLM requests add_connector, sidecar executes, returns result, final_stream gives the assistant reply. Good — same shape, just route some tool calls to native handlers.

# Design: MCP Connector Integration for The Living Studio

**Date:** 2026-10-21
**Topic:** Expose the existing MCP *client* connectors in the Living Studio (config, UI, conversational suggestions)
**Status:** Draft → build (approved by human in chat)

## What exists today

The `packages/connectors/` package already implements the MCP **client** side of
this story:

- `mcp/connector.py` — `MCPClientConnector` using `fastmcp.Client` over HTTP,
  with `${VAR}` credential expansion and OAuth token support.
- `catalog.py` — 16 curated presets across 5 capability areas, with
  `get_preset`, `list_presets(area)`, `connector_config_from_preset`.
- `registry.py` — `ConnectorRegistry`, JSON-backed, read/write of `connectors.json`.
- `factory.py` — `build_connector(ConnectorConfig)`.
- CLI `connectors list|catalog|add|health|ingest` in `apps/cli/src/.../connectors.py`.
- `docs/connectors.md` documents the CLI flow.

The gap is the **Studio side**: the sidecar (`apps/studio-api`) has no connector
routes; `SettingsPanel.tsx` only shows *simulated* MCP sources; and the chat
engine (`studio/chat.py`) connects to a single ODI `mcp_url` and cannot surface
or wire a connector. This design fills that gap without re-architecting the
connectors package.

## Intent & why

Let a PM connect an external MCP server (search, analytics, CRM, etc.) as a
data source for ODI — from the Studio UI, or by asking the copilot in conversation —
and have the choice persist to a shared background config file used by both the
CLI and the Studio. "Modular" = keep using the existing `Connector` protocol and
preset catalog; just surface it in two new places (Studio settings + chat).

## Goals / non-goals / anti-goals

- Goals:
  - Shared background config file (CLI + Studio + Tauri all agree on the path).
  - Studio UI: list configured connectors + live health, add from a curated
    "Recommended" preset subset, add a custom URL, remove.
  - Conversational: the copilot can *suggest and wire* a connector via a
    sidecar-native tool call (your answer 2), surfaced as a UI suggestion card.
- Non-goals:
  - Auto-discovery/marketplace manifest fetching (your answer 3: presets are the
    recommended set; a separate "add custom" experience covers self-hosted /
    external-marketplace servers). Defer live external marketplace discovery.
  - Ingest-from-Studio mapping onto ODI artifacts (already deferred in roadmap).
  - Making the ODI *server* expose connector tools (the sidecar owns config,
    not the ODI server).
- Anti-goal: do not couple the ODI server to the connectors package.

## Locked decisions (from the human)

1. **Shared config file:** sidecar and CLI share one file.
2. **Conversational behavior:** the LLM *calls a sidecar tool* to register/wire a
   connector inline (one chat turn), not just text-suggest.
3. **Marketplaces:** the most prominent hosted MCP servers are surfaced as easy
   presets; users can still add arbitrary servers via a "add custom" flow.

## Defaults decided by me (flagged)

- **Config location:** `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_FILE` env →
  `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/agentic-odi/connectors.json` (fallback `~/.config/agentic-odi/connectors.json`).
  This matches the existing `llm_profile.json` XDG location and works regardless of
  cwd (important for the Tauri sidecar). The CLI default changes from cwd-relative
  `.agentic-odi/connectors.json` to this resolver; CLI tests use `--config`/tmp so
  they are unaffected. I'll update `docs/connectors.md` to match.
- **Recommended subset:** I'll add an `is_recommended: bool = False` field to
  `ConnectorPreset` and mark these (prominent, mostly API-key or OAuth-hosted):
  `exa`, `tavily`, `posthog`, `amplitude`, `github`, `linear`, `slack`. The CLI
  `connectors catalog` gains a `--recommended` flag too. (Call to confirm below.)
- **MIT copyright:** `Copyright (c) 2026 Agentic ODI contributors` (already applied
  in PR #54).

## Architecture

```text
                                         ┌──────────────────────────────┐
  Living Studio SPA (settings &         │ agentic_odi_studio_api       │
  connector cards) ── /api/connectors ─▶│ - studio/connectors.py  (NEW)  │
                                      │   list/add/remove/health on the│
                                      │   shared ConnectorRegistry        │
                                      │ - studio/router.py        (EXT)   │
                                      │   GET/POST/DELETE endpoints       │
  ┌───────────────────┐ /api/chat      │ - studio/chat.py       (EXT)    │
  │   ChatCopilot     │ SSE:           │   native tool-call: add_connector│
  │  suggestion card  │ connector event│   → registry.write + health     │
  └───────────────────┘ canvas_dirty   └──────────┬──────────────────────┘
                                  MCP/HTTP ▼        │
                            mcp_server (:8000)      ▼
                                  connectors package (catalog/presets),
                                  shared connectors.json (~/.config/agentic-odi/)
```

The ODI `mcp_server` is untouched. The sidecar owns connector config + health.

## Sidecar: `studio/connectors.py` (new)

A thin service layer over the existing connectors package; importable and
unit-testable without HTTP:

- `connectors_file() -> Path` — delegates to a new
  `agentic_odi_connectors.paths.connectors_file()` resolver (shared with CLI).
- `list_connectors() -> list[ConnectorConfig]`
- `list_catalog(area: str | None = None, recommended: bool = False) -> list[ConnectorPreset]`
- `add_from_preset(preset_id, name=None) -> AddedConnector` (registers via
  `connector_config_from_preset` + `ConnectorRegistry.add`, then runs
  `connector.health()` and includes the result)
- `add_manual(name, url, headers=None) -> AddedConnector`
- `remove_connector(name) -> None`
- `health(name) -> HealthStatus` (builds the connector and awaits `health()`)

`AddedConnector` = `{config, health}`. Health failures (missing env, unreachable)
are caught and returned (not raised), so the UI shows a red dot + message.

## Sidecar: `router.py` (extend)

- `GET /api/connectors` → `list_connectors()`
- `GET /api/connectors/catalog?area=&recommended=` → presets
- `POST /api/connectors` body `{preset_id? | name+url+headers?}` → add (returns
  `{ok, name, kind, health}`)
- `DELETE /api/connectors/{name}` → remove
- `POST /api/connectors/{name}/health` → `{ok, message, details}`

Routes resolve the file per-request (stateless); env override works for tests and
Tauri.

## Chat engine: `studio/chat.py` (extend)

Today `stream_chat` builds LLM tools from `mcp_client.list_tools()` (ODI tools)
only. Extension:

- Define two **sidecar-native** tool schemas (NOT on the ODI server):
  `add_connector_from_preset(preset_id, name?)` and `add_connector_manual(name,
  url, headers?)`. Append them to the OpenAI `tools` list alongside the MCP tools.
- When the LLM emits tool_calls, branch: if `name` is a native tool, execute it
  via `connectors.add_from_preset`/`add_manual` (locally, no `mcp_client`); else
  `mcp_client.call_tool(...)`.
- On a successful native add, yield a new SSE event `connector` carrying
  `{name, preset_id?, health}` so the UI renders a "Connected" card / toast, then
  feed the human-readable result back into `messages` and continue to the final
  stream as today.
- The LLM is primed in `SYSTEM_PROMPT` to offer to connect an external source
  when the user mentions one it knows (e.g., "Gong call" → suggest the `gong`
  preset). It only calls the tool when the user consents in the same turn.

One tool-call round (same shape as today); no multi-turn agentic loop added.

## Frontend

- `types.ts`: add `ConnectorConfig`, `ConnectorPreset`, `ConnectorHealth`,
  `ConnectorSuggestion` (with `area`, `preset_id`).
- `studioApi.ts`: `listConnectors`, `listPresets`, `addConnectorPreset`,
  `addConnectorManual`, `removeConnector`, `healthConnector`.
- `sse.ts`: already generic `event + data`; extend `RawSseEvent`-handling in
  `StudioContext` to read a new `connector` event type.
- `StudioContext.tsx`: add `connectors`, `presets`, and `addConnector*` state +
  handlers; on `connector` SSE event, push a toast + refresh the connectors list.
- `SettingsPanel.tsx`: new "Connectors" section —
  - "Recommended" preset cards (the `is_recommended` subset) with Connect buttons;
  - configured list with 🟢/🔴 health dots and ✕ remove;
  - "Add custom" form (name, url, optional `KEY=VALUE` headers).
- `ChatCopilot.tsx`: render a `connector` suggestion card in the chat log (next to
  `toolActivity`) showing the wired connector + health, so the conversational flow
  is visible.

## Tests (mirror existing conventions)

- `apps/studio-api/tests/test_studio_connectors.py`: TestClient over
  `create_app`, monkeypatch the connectors file to a tmp path (env), exercise
  list/catalog/add/remove/health; assert 200s and JSON shape. Native `add` uses an
  in-memory-ish health (registry round-trips config; health may be `ok=False` for
  unreachable — assert the response shape, not reachability).
- `apps/studio-api/tests/test_studio_chat_connectors.py`: monkeypatch the LLM
  client's completion to emit a tool_call naming `add_connector_from_preset`, then
  assert a `connector` SSE event is yielded with the preset id and a `message`
  frame.
- `apps/studio/src/api/studio_connectors.test.ts` (+ extend `sse.test.ts`):
  fetch-wrapper shapes and the `connector` SSE parse.
- `packages/connectors/tests/test_paths.py` + extend `test_catalog.py`
  (`is_recommended`/`list_presets(recommended=True)`) — minimal.
- Keep using in-memory `FastMCP` servers where connectors are tested; never hit
  real external endpoints in unit tests.

Lint/types: `uv run ruff check . && uv run mypy apps packages`; pytest per
`.agents/workflows/test.md`; `npm --prefix studio run test`.

## Docs (same task)

- `docs/connectors.md`: add a "From The Living Studio" section + update the shared
  config location to the XDG path.
- `docs/living-studio.md`: note the Connectors settings section.
- `README.md` (new-structure README in the active branch): Connectors already
  listed under Code Overview; keep in sync.

## Risks / open questions (theirs to answer before build, if any)

- (Q) Is the recommended preset subset acceptable, or do you want a different
  set / a different name for the subset?
- (Q) Config location: XDG `~/.config/agentic-odi/connectors.json` shared with a
  CLI default change — acceptable, or keep the CLI cwd-relative default and only
  use XDG from the sidecar?
- (Q) Conversational consent: should the copilot *call* the add tool directly when
  it's confident, or always first propose and wait for an explicit "yes"?

# Skill: writing-plans

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write implementation plans for an engineer who has not seen this codebase or this spec. Assume they write idiomatic code in the project's language once they know the exact interface and the exact test, and that they will make a reasonable choice wherever the plan leaves one open. What they cannot know is what you decided: which files, which names and signatures, which values from the spec, which tests prove each task. Document those. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Task Right-Sizing

A task is the smallest unit that carries its own test cycle and is worth a
fresh reviewer's gate. When drawing task boundaries: fold setup,
configuration, scaffolding, and documentation steps into the task whose
deliverable needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully
reject one task while approving its neighbor. Each task ends with an
independently testable deliverable.

## Step Granularity

**Each step is one action with a checkable result:**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

**Spec:** [path to the spec/design doc this plan implements — the plan
argues from the spec, so the spec travels with it; executors read both]

## Global Constraints

[The spec's project-wide requirements — version floors, dependency limits,
naming and copy rules, platform requirements — one line each, with exact
values copied verbatim from the spec. Every task's requirements implicitly
include this section.]

## Review Focus

[The five input classes or failure modes the spec implies but no task's
tests exercise that are most likely to bite a person using this software
— one line each, naming the input or condition and the behavior a
reasonable person would expect, most likely first. The spec is a vision
document: it says what the software must do, not everything it will
meet, and its silence on an input is not permission for that input to
break the program. Write the list here, once, with the spec in front of
you. Then, for each line, add the test that pins it to the task that
owns the code, in that task's own step style.]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: [what this task uses from earlier tasks — exact signatures]
- Produces: [what later tasks rely on — exact function names, parameter
  and return types. A task's implementer sees only their own task; this
  block is how they learn the names and types neighboring tasks use.]

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement `function(input: InputType) -> ResultType` in `exact/path/to/file.py`**

One line on the approach when the signature and the test leave a choice
(which library call, which data structure); a code block only for an
algorithm they do not determine.

- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## What a Step Contains

A step is done when the implementer can write exactly one reasonable thing
from it. That is the whole requirement: unambiguous, not complete. Each kind
of step carries what makes it unambiguous and nothing more:

- **A test step:** the test's name and its assertions, as code, with the
  spec's exact values in them.
- **A code step:** the exact signature (name, parameters, return type), the
  file it lives in, and the specific values the spec pins. The implementer
  writes the body. A body appears only for an algorithm the signature and
  tests do not determine, or for exact copy the spec fixes.
- **A verification step:** the command to run and the output that means it
  passed.
- **A reference to another task:** that task's Interfaces block says what
  to use; the plan does not repeat that task's code.

A plan is the set of decisions the implementer cannot make alone. A plan
longer than the code it describes has written the code instead. Lines that
decide nothing ("TBD", "handle edge cases", "add appropriate validation",
"write tests for the above", a type or function no task defines) are the
opposite failure, and the self-review catches both.

## Self-Review

After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.

**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.

**2. Step scan:** Every step must let the implementer write exactly one reasonable thing, and no step may carry more than that: a line that decides nothing is a gap, a function body the signature and tests already determine is a transcript. Fix both.

**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.

**4. Review Focus:** For each input class or failure mode the spec implies, is there a task whose tests exercise it? The five uncovered ones most likely to bite a person go in the Review Focus section, and each line there gets its test added to the owning task. An empty section means you checked and found none, not that you skipped the check.

**5. Proportion:** Compare the plan's length to the spec's. A plan several times longer than the spec it implements is a transcript of the program, not a plan. If code blocks are most of the document, replace bodies with signatures, test names and assertions, and check that each step is still unambiguous.

If you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.

## Execution Handoff

After saving and self-reviewing the plan, link it for your human partner
to read. If they have already explicitly supplied an execution method, ask
them to review the plan and confirm it captures what they want; wait for that
review before implementation, then use the preserved method. Otherwise, ask
them to review the plan and choose an execution method before implementation.

**When no execution method has already been supplied:**

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Please review the plan. Which execution approach would you prefer?**

- **Subagent-driven** - A fresh subagent implements each task and a fresh reviewer checks it before the next one starts, then a whole-branch review at the end. Most thorough; costs a fresh context per task and per review.
- **Native** - I implement every task myself in this session, the way this harness runs work, then one fresh reviewer on the most capable model checks the whole branch. Cheapest and fastest; no independent review until the end. Runs well with a mid-tier session model, since the plan carries the design.

**For this plan I recommend <one of the two>, because <one sentence from the plan: how much the tasks depend on each other's interfaces, how many there are, what a shipped mistake would cost>. Does the plan capture what you want, and which approach should we use?"**

**When an execution method has already been supplied:**

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Please review the plan. Does it capture what you want?"**

**If Subagent-driven chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development

**If Native chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:executing-plans
